Morgan (support): Customer ACME opened an escalation: intermittent 400s with 'embedding dim mismatch' + sporadic tail latencies >2.5s on /v1/embeddings. Spike observed ~2026-03-05T14:12Z. They say client uses dynamic batching and max_batch_size=256. Attached sample payload + request ids.

Sam H: Can you paste the raw request body & the example request-id/trace id? Also which model variant are they calling (open-embed-2.3 vs open-embed-2.3-q2)?

Morgan (support): Sample request (redacted):
```json
{"model":"open-embed-2.3-q2","input":["short text", "a much longer piece of text...", "another"], "client_max_batch_size":256}
```
They also sent this error from our logs:
```
2026-03-05T14:12:07Z shard-3 ERROR request=req_abc123 embedding: unexpected vector len 1536 != expected 1024 (route=open-embed-2.3, variant=q2)
2026-03-05T14:12:07Z shard-3 WARN batch_coalesce dropped request=req_def456 reason=dim-mismatch
2026-03-05T14:12:08Z router ERROR fallback failed for req_ghi789: incompatible-variant
```

Ingrid T: That looks like mixed-model routing. If dynamic batching coalesced requests across model variants (e.g., q2 vs base), we can see dim mismatches. Do we have evidence of cross-variant coalescing?

dynbatch-bot: telemetry:coalesce_window_ms=8, max_batch_size=256, pad_to_max=false, route_policy=latency_cost_hybrid, shard=3

Sam H: Two quick checks: 1) confirm the client's model name exactly matches the route (typo could route to fallback variant). 2) check whether the route policy allowed fallback to open-embed-2.3 (non-q2) during capacity pressure. If so, mixed dims explain the 1536 vs 1024.

Morgan (support): Customer guarantees they requested q2, but their SDK version is old. Also they have varied payload sizes (some single sentences, some paragraphs) which could lead to coalescing delay + large batches. They attached client trace ids: req_abc123, req_def456, req_ghi789.

Lee (infra): Looking at router traces for shard-3 around those ids: I see a recent autoscaler bump at 14:11:55 and a config push at 14:10 that changed coalesce_window_ms from 5->8ms and increased max_batch_size from 128->256 for a burst policy. That timing lines up. Coalescing window + larger max batch combined with route fallback could cause mixing of variants during capacity fallback.

Lee (infra): Quick mitigations we can try:
- rollback the burst config (max_batch_size -> 128, coalesce_window_ms -> 5)
- pin routing to respect model variant label (no fallback across quantization variants)
- ask customer to set client_max_batch_size=64 or disable client-side dynamic batching temporarily

Sam H: For the customer-facing repro steps to try now:
1) Pin model in request to exact variant: `model=open-embed-2.3-q2`
2) Set `client_max_batch_size=64` or remove large-batch cap 256
3) Send a mixed-size payload set (their sample) 20x and capture request-ids
4) If they still see 400s, collect route traces + the `router.trace_id` header and forward to eng-infra

Morgan (support): I told the customer to try pinning the model + lower client batch size and to capture 5 failing request-ids if it recurs. They've scheduled a call in 30m.

Ingrid T: Long-term fix: router should never coalesce across incompatible model shapes. We need a router change: tag model variants with a shape signature and use it as part of coalescing key. Also improve telemetry to emit "coalesced-variant-mix" metrics. I'll file a runtime ticket.

Sam H: Also check whether pad_to_max behavior interacts: if pad_to_max=true we'll introduce padding vectors which can mask dim mismatches for some cases but inflate cost. Customer currently had pad_to_max=false per telemetry.

Lee (infra): I'm going to roll back the burst config in 10m unless we have reason not to. If rollback resolves errors and tail latency, that confirms coalesce-window + max_batch_size interaction.

dynbatch-bot: action:schedule rollback at 2026-03-05T14:20Z by Lee; notify #eng-runtime on completion.

Morgan (support): I'll keep the customer updated on the call. If rollback doesn't fix it, we'll capture full router traces and escalate to eng-runtime for a hotfix.

Sam H: Thanks. Capture all request ids and the customer's SDK version. Also note the billing impact: larger batches briefly increased per-token compute usage — finance might want a heads-up if we revert to smaller batches for a tenant with reserved capacity.

Morgan (support): Call in progress; customer confirmed that after pinning to q2 + lowering client batch size to 64 they saw no dim errors in 2 test runs but tail latency still had a single 1.8s spike (down from 2.5s). Keeping the thread updated.

Lee (infra): Rollback complete at 2026-03-05T14:21Z. Early telemetry shows coalesce_window_ms back to 5 and max_batch_size=128 on shard-3. Will watch metrics for 15m.

Sam H: Great. If errors don't reappear in 15m and customer is happy, we'll close. Otherwise escalate to eng-runtime with full traces.

Morgan (support): Customer happy for now. Closing pending observation window. Follow-ups: Ingrid to file runtime ticket for variant-shape key; Lee to monitor shard-3 for 24h.

Ingrid T: Ticket created: RUNTIME-4629 "router: disallow coalescing across incompatible model shapes". Assigned to eng-runtime.

Morgan (support): Marking resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
